verdict.rationale: Windows is an OS that runs on the user's own hardware. Community reports describe setting up Windows 10 and Windows Server 2019 on one's own machines (windows-comm-10). They also note that a local, offline account is still possible during setup, though only through workarounds such as disconnecting from the internet (windows-comm-6). Self-hosting is therefore inherent, but users report friction pushing them toward a Microsoft-hosted account (windows-comm-8), and no first-party docs address self-hosted deployment. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of self-hosted or offline deployment, a documented supported path to run without a Microsoft account, and evidence of self-hosted management or update infrastructure.
